Impending

im-PEND-ing — the root means 'to hang'; something impending hangs over you, about to happen. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Impending is about to happen or occur, used for something threatening or unwelcome.

Dark storm clouds gathering on the horizon signaled the impending hurricane.

Worked Example

Factory workers notice their supervisors holding unusually long, quiet meetings behind closed doors for three days straight, and by the end of the week, everyone in the building has heard the same unconfirmed rumor about company-wide cuts.

Sensing that something serious is about to happen, even before it's officially announced, is exactly what impending means. Impending is a close cousin of imminent (both mean 'about to happen'), though impending often carries a slightly more ominous, threatening tone.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

imminent: about to happen very soon

approaching: coming closer, soon to arrive

looming: appearing as an imminent, often threatening, presence

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

distant: far off in time or space

remote: unlikely to happen soon, or far removed

Where it sits · how threatening the coming event feels — approaching → impending → looming

approaching vs. impending: Approaching is more neutral than impending -- approaching can describe anything getting closer, good or bad, while impending usually carries a sense that something serious or threatening is coming.

looming vs. impending: Looming can feel even more ominous than impending: impending simply means something is about to happen, but looming often adds a sense of dread, like a shadow growing larger.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — im- (in-)

prefix — im- (in-): upon, over (Latin)

root — -pend-

root — -pend-: to hang (Latin (pendere))

suffix — -ing

suffix — -ing: forming an adjective from a verb (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin im- ('upon, over') plus pendere ('to hang'), with the -ing ending turning the verb into an adjective. Something impending literally hangs over the present moment, about to fall.

Use the root in a new word: pendant

Use the root in a new word: pendant: She wore a small silver pendant that had belonged to her grandmother.
